      "severity": "high",
      "title": "1. BLOCKING: Concurrent starts can overwrite broker ownership",
      "body": "Two callers can both read no broker before taking the lock.       "file": "plugins/codex/scripts/lib/broker-lifecycle.mjs",
      "line_start": 289,
      "line_end": 308,
      "confidence": 0.96,
      "recommendation": "Re-read and claim the broker record inside the lock, and guard every later save or replacement by that claim."
    },
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "title": "2. BLOCKING: SessionEnd can discard a starting broker",
      "body": "SessionEnd snapshots a starting record with pid:null before the spawn finishes. If that broker becomes ready and acknowledges shutdown but remains alive, teardown uses the old null PID, returns no-pid with kept:false, removes its files, and clears even a same-endpoint record that has since gained a PID and identity.",
      "file": "plugins/codex/scripts/session-lifecycle-hook.mjs",
      "line_start": 348,
      "line_end": 375,
      "confidence": 0.91,
      "recommendation": "Re-read broker ownership before teardown and keep a null-PID record until exit or replacement is proved."
    },
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "title": "3. BLOCKING: Failed-start cleanup treats refusal or signal delivery as resolution",
      "body": "If the Windows identity probe returns null for a live failed-start child, the verified kill refuses, yet teardown attempts to remove its files; a later stale replacement clears its record. On POSIX, a delivered SIGTERM sets signalled even if the child ignores it, so this branch clears the record immediately. Either path can leave a live broker without usable ownership state.",
      "file": "plugins/codex/scripts/lib/broker-lifecycle.mjs",
      "line_start": 319,
      "line_end": 335,
      "confidence": 0.92,
      "recommendation": "Retain the record and files until the child and its subtree are confirmed gone; retry identity capture while the child handle is live."
    },
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "title": "4. BLOCKING: Exit 241 can miss a living grandchild",
      "body": "The vanished-root query finds only processes whose immediate ParentProcessId equals the worker PID. If the worker and its direct child exit between the reaper check and the kill, but a grandchild remains, the query emits no survivors. cancelDecision then treats 241 as clean and writes cancelled despite a living descendant.",
      "file": "plugins/codex/scripts/lib/process.mjs",
      "line_start": 482,
      "line_end": 495,
      "confidence": 0.88,
      "recommendation": "Treat an empty direct-parent query as unknown unless complete ancestry or prior tree evidence proves the subtree gone."
    },
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "title": "5. BLOCKING: An interrupt ACK can erase a terminal outcome",
      "body": "interrupted:true means the turn/interrupt RPC answered; it does not prove the worker's later terminal transition was caused by cancel. If the worker completes or a reaper records failure before this write, causedByCancel bypasses the terminal guard and replaces that outcome with cancelled, masking the result or error on both platforms.",
      "file": "plugins/codex/scripts/lib/job-control.mjs",
      "line_start": 334,
      "line_end": 352,
      "confidence": 0.92,
      "recommendation": "Preserve an already terminal record unless its transition is explicitly correlated with this cancellation."
    }
  ],
  "next_steps": [
    "Fix these paths, add concurrent-start and failed-start interleaving checks, then rerun Windows and POSIX end-to-end validation."
  ]
}

If that broker becomes ready and acknowledges shutdown but remains alive, teardown uses the old null PID, returns no-pid with kept:false, removes its files, and clears even a same-endpoint record that has since gained a PID and identity.
findings.recommendation: Re-read broker ownership before teardown and keep a null-PID record until exit or replacement is proved.

findings.title: 3. BLOCKING: Failed-start cleanup treats refusal or signal delivery as resolution
findings.body: If the Windows identity probe returns null for a live failed-start child, the verified kill refuses, yet teardown attempts to remove its files; a later stale replacement clears its record. On POSIX, a delivered SIGTERM sets signalled even if the child ignores it, so this branch clears the record immediately. Either path can leave a live broker without usable ownership state.
findings.recommendation: Retain the record and files until the child and its subtree are confirmed gone; retry identity capture while the child handle is live.

findings.title: 4. BLOCKING: Exit 241 can miss a living grandchild
findings.body: The vanished-root query finds only processes whose immediate ParentProcessId equals the worker PID. If the worker and its direct child exit between the reaper check and the kill, but a grandchild remains, the query emits no survivors. cancelDecision then treats 241 as clean and writes cancelled despite a living descendant.
findings.recommendation: Treat an empty direct-parent query as unknown unless complete ancestry or prior tree evidence proves the subtree gone.

findings.title: 5. BLOCKING: An interrupt ACK can erase a terminal outcome
findings.body: interrupted:true means the turn/interrupt RPC answered; it does not prove the worker's later terminal transition was caused by cancel. If the worker completes or a reaper records failure before this write, causedByCancel bypasses the terminal guard and replaces that outcome with cancelled, masking the result or error on both platforms.
findings.recommendation: Preserve an already terminal record unless its transition is explicitly correlated with this cancellation.

storedJob.rendered:
# Codex Adversarial Review

Target: branch diff against main
Verdict: needs-attention

DO-NOT-SHIP. Pass 5 still has broker ownership races and paths that report cancellation without proving the process tree stopped.

Findings:
- [high] 1. BLOCKING: Concurrent starts can overwrite broker ownership (plugins/codex/scripts/lib/broker-lifecycle.mjs:289-308)
  Two callers can both read no broker before taking the lock. Each then unconditionally writes a starting record and spawns under that lock; later identity and ready-record saves are also unconditional. Both brokers can remain live while broker.json names only one. A worker kill can then include the unrecorded broker in its tree.
  Recommendation: Re-read and claim the broker record inside the lock, and guard every later save or replacement by that claim.
- [high] 2. BLOCKING: SessionEnd can discard a starting broker (plugins/codex/scripts/session-lifecycle-hook.mjs:348-375)
  SessionEnd snapshots a starting record with pid:null before the spawn finishes. If that broker becomes ready and acknowledges shutdown but remains alive, teardown uses the old null PID, returns no-pid with kept:false, removes its files, and clears even a same-endpoint record that has since gained a PID and identity.
  Recommendation: Re-read broker ownership before teardown and keep a null-PID record until exit or replacement is proved.
- [high] 3. BLOCKING: Failed-start cleanup treats refusal or signal delivery as resolution (plugins/codex/scripts/lib/broker-lifecycle.mjs:319-335)
  If the Windows identity probe returns null for a live failed-start child, the verified kill refuses, yet teardown attempts to remove its files; a later stale replacement clears its record. On POSIX, a delivered SIGTERM sets signalled even if the child ignores it, so this branch clears the record immediately. Either path can leave a live broker without usable ownership state.
  Recommendation: Retain the record and files until the child and its subtree are confirmed gone; retry identity capture while the child handle is live.
- [high] 4. BLOCKING: Exit 241 can miss a living grandchild (plugins/codex/scripts/lib/process.mjs:482-495)
  The vanished-root query finds only processes whose immediate ParentProcessId equals the worker PID. If the worker and its direct child exit between the reaper check and the kill, but a grandchild remains, the query emits no survivors. cancelDecision then treats 241 as clean and writes cancelled despite a living descendant.
  Recommendation: Treat an empty direct-parent query as unknown unless complete ancestry or prior tree evidence proves the subtree gone.
- [high] 5. BLOCKING: An interrupt ACK can erase a terminal outcome (plugins/codex/scripts/lib/job-control.mjs:334-352)
  interrupted:true means the turn/interrupt RPC answered; it does not prove the worker's later terminal transition was caused by cancel. If the worker completes or a reaper records failure before this write, causedByCancel bypasses the terminal guard and replaces that outcome with cancelled, masking the result or error on both platforms.
  Recommendation: Preserve an already terminal record unless its transition is explicitly correlated with this cancellation.

Next steps:
- Fix these paths, add concurrent-start and failed-start interleaving checks, then rerun Windows and POSIX end-to-end validation.
